# 1. Introduction
This analysis uses linear regression to examine the relationships between the CAD/JPY exchange rate and macroeconomic indicators in Canada and Japan.


# 2. Libraries
```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
```


# 3. Data Loading
```{r load_data}
# Load processed data
df <- read.csv("processed_data.csv")
```


# 4. Simple Linear Regression
```{r simple_linear_regression}
# GDP
model_gdp_ca <- lm(cad_jpy ~ gdp_CA, data = df)
model_gdp_jp <- lm(cad_jpy ~ gdp_JP, data = df)


# Inflation rate
model_infl_ca <- lm(cad_jpy ~ infl_CA, data = df)
model_infl_jp <- lm(cad_jpy ~ infl_JP, data = df)


# Unemployment rate
model_unemp_ca <- lm(cad_jpy ~ unemp_CA, data = df)
model_unemp_jp <- lm(cad_jpy ~ unemp_JP, data = df)


# Combine models
simple_models <- list(
  "GDP - Canada" = model_gdp_ca,
  "GDP - Japan" = model_gdp_jp,
  "Inflation - Canada" = model_infl_ca,
  "Inflation - Japan" = model_infl_jp,
  "Unemployment - Canada" = model_unemp_ca,
  "Unemployment - Japan" = model_unemp_jp
)


# Summarize regression results
simple_results <- data.frame(
  Model = names(simple_models),
  R_Squared = sapply(simple_models, function(m) summary(m)$r.squared),
  P_Value = sapply(simple_models, function(m) summary(m)$coefficients[2, 4])
)


knitr::kable(simple_results, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```



# 5. Multiple Linear Regression
```{r multiple_linear_regression}
# Canada
model_ca <- lm(
  cad_jpy ~ gdp_CA + infl_CA + unemp_CA,
  data = df
)


# Japan
model_jp <- lm(
  cad_jpy ~ gdp_JP + infl_JP + unemp_JP,
  data = df
)


# Compare model performance
multiple_models <- list(
  "Canada" = model_ca,
  "Japan" = model_jp
)

multiple_results <- data.frame(
  Model = names(multiple_models),
  R_Squared = sapply(multiple_models, function(m) summary(m)$r.squared),
  Adjusted_R_Squared = sapply(multiple_models, function(m) summary(m)$adj.r.squared),
  P_Value = sapply(multiple_models, function(m) {
    f <- summary(m)$fstatistic
    pf(f[1], f[2], f[3], lower.tail = FALSE)
  })
)


knitr::kable(multiple_results, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```


# 6. Model Comparison
```{r model_comparison}
# Candidate models
model_1 <- model_ca
model_2 <- model_jp

model_3 <- lm(
  cad_jpy ~ gdp_CA + infl_CA + unemp_CA +
    gdp_JP + infl_JP + unemp_JP,
  data = df
)

model_4 <- lm(
  cad_jpy ~ gdp_JP + infl_JP + infl_CA + unemp_CA,
  data = df
)

model_5 <- lm(
  cad_jpy ~ gdp_JP + infl_JP + unemp_CA,
  data = df
)

model_6 <- lm(
  cad_jpy ~ gdp_JP + infl_JP + unemp_JP + unemp_CA,
  data = df
)


# Compare models using AIC
aic_results <- AIC(
  model_1, model_2, model_3,
  model_4, model_5, model_6
)


knitr::kable(aic_results, digits = 3)
```


# 7. Final Model
Although the six-variable model achieved the lowest AIC, the Japan-only model was selected to prioritize simplicity given the small sample size of 20 annual observations.
## 7.1 Regression Results
```{r final_model}
# Select the final model
final_model <- model_2


# Display regression results
summary(final_model)
```


## 7.2 Actual vs Fitted CAD/JPY
```{r actual_vs_fitted}
# Calculate fitted values
df$fitted_cad_jpy <- fitted(final_model)

# Compare actual and fitted exchange rates
ggplot(df, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cad_jpy, color = "Actual"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = fitted_cad_jpy, color = "Fitted"),
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Actual vs Fitted CAD/JPY Exchange Rate",
    x = "Year",
    y = "CAD/JPY",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Actual" = "gray", "Fitted" = "green")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


## 7.3 Model Diagnostics
```{r model_diagnostics, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
# Diagnostic plots
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

plot(final_model)


# Reset plot layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```



# 8. Summary
Japan's GDP, inflation rate, and unemployment rate were statistically significant in the final multiple regression model, which explained approximately 69.2% of the variation in CAD/JPY exchange rates (R² = 0.6923).

Although the six-variable model had the lowest AIC, the Japan-only model was selected for its simplicity. The small sample size and potential outliers limit the reliability of the results.
